 Second screwworm case confirmed miles from first Texas detection
 

 New infection found in one-month-old calf in same county

 

 
 
 
 
 8 June 2026
 
 

 
 
 
 1 minute read
 
 

 
 
 
 By: Global Ag Media 
 

 

 
 
 
 
 North America

 

 

 

 

 A second case of the flesh-eating screwworm parasite was confirmed in Texas by the US Department of Agriculture on Friday, emerging just miles from where the first US detection in decades was reported this week, reported Reuters. 

The new case in Zavala County was detected on a ranch 5.6 miles (9 km) from the first positive case of screwworm in Texas, which the USDA confirmed on Wednesday.

The infection, which the USDA said was in a one-month-old calf, was reported earlier on Friday by Reuters, citing sources.

The USDA discovered the second infestation "after testing a number of suspect cases," the department's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service said in a press release.

APHIS and Texas Animal Health Commission officials are continuing to "collect and test other samples from the surrounding area which have come back negative," it said.

Friday's case and the initial detection in nearby La Pryor, a town roughly 30 miles (50 km) northeast of the US-Mexico border, have dealt a setback to US cattle ranchers, who have been preparing for the arrival of the pest as it has moved north through Mexico over the past year.

Screwworms are parasitic flies that deposit eggs in open wounds or mucous membranes of warm-blooded animals. After hatching, the larvae penetrate living tissue, feeding on the host and potentially causing fatal damage if not treated.

An outbreak in US border states in the 1960s devastated wildlife and inflicted heavy financial losses on ranchers.

A widespread resurgence now could pose a significant economic threat in Texas, the country’s largest cattle-producing state, through animal deaths as well as higher labour and treatment costs.

To limit the risk, Washington has kept the US-Mexico border closed to live cattle imports for more than a year and has spent millions of dollars to curb the pest’s northward spread, including funding sterile fly production, expanding trapping programs and stepping up livestock monitoring.

translationZh:
美国农业部周五在得克萨斯州确认了第二例食肉螺旋蝇寄生虫病例，该病例出现在本周早些时候美国数十年来首例发现地仅数英里之外，据路透社报道。

萨瓦拉县的新病例是在一处牧场发现的，距离美国农业部周三确认的得州首例螺旋蝇阳性病例5.6英里（9公里）。

美国农业部称，感染发生在一头一个月大的小牛身上，路透社周五早些时候援引消息来源报道了这一情况。

美国农业部动植物卫生检验局在一份新闻稿中表示，该部门在“检测了若干疑似病例后”发现了第二起感染。

APHIS和得州动物卫生委员会的官员正在继续“收集并检测周边地区的其他样本，这些样本结果均为阴性”。

周五的病例以及最初在拉普赖尔（La Pryor）附近发现的病例——该镇距美墨边境约30英里（50公里）东北方向——对美国养牛户造成了打击，他们一直在为这种害虫的到来做准备，因为过去一年它已通过墨西哥向北移动。

螺旋蝇是一种寄生蝇，会在温血动物的开放性伤口或粘膜上产卵。幼虫孵化后，钻入活体组织，以宿主为食，若不治疗可能造成致命伤害。

20世纪60年代美国边境各州的疫情曾对野生动物造成毁灭性打击，并给牧场主带来沉重经济损失。

如今若再次大规模暴发，可能对得克萨斯州——美国最大的养牛州——构成重大经济威胁，包括动物死亡以及劳动力和治疗成本上升。

为降低风险，美国政府已关闭美墨边境活牛进口超过一年，并投入数百万美元遏制虫害北扩，包括资助不育蝇生产、扩大诱捕计划以及加强牲畜监测。
